news.title: JPMorgan Takes Bank Deposit Tokens Toward Ethereum for Institutional Settlement
news.body: JPMorgan said JPM Coin would become available to institutional clients on Ethereum for blockchain payments, tokenized-asset settlement and collateralization. The extension brings commercial-bank money onto public blockchain infrastructure, but JPM Coin remains a deposit token rather than a stablecoin, with different eligibility and legal claims. Institutional treasury teams evaluating it must map eligible counterparties and supported settlement workflows before moving funds.

news.title: Ramp Seeks Custody and Investment Powers Without Becoming a Deposit Bank
news.body: Ramp applied to the OCC to establish a national trust bank for fiduciary investment management and digital-asset custody, without accepting deposits or making commercial loans. Approval would let Ramp bring those activities under its own charter, not replace the banking partners supporting its broader business. For those partners, the practical question is how Ramp would divide custody, investment management and banking responsibilities under any OCC operating conditions.

news.title: Relay and Nium Reach $500 Million Through Embedded Cross-Border Payments
news.body: Relay and Nium reported more than $500 million in cross-border payments across 153 countries during approximately their partnership’s first year, with more than 500 Relay customers currently using the service. Relay adds international transfers inside its business-banking interface, while Nium gains distribution without acquiring each SMB directly. The next commercial test is whether customer growth and repeat payments broaden that volume beyond a concentrated group of businesses and corridors.

news.title: Fiserv Bundles Global Acquiring and Local Payment Methods Through Commerce Hub
news.body: Fiserv announced global availability of Commerce Hub, combining acquiring, market-specific payment methods and commerce services through one connection. The common integration gives enterprise merchants and marketplaces an alternative to assembling separate connections; Klarna’s integration accompanies a distinct rollout to 100,000 U.S. physical merchant locations through Clover. Merchants evaluating migration should compare country-level payment coverage and integration requirements, rather than treat Clover’s location count as Commerce Hub adoption.

news.title: Square Consolidates Card Processing on Marqeta With Business Credit Migration
news.body: Square migrated its existing business credit-card program to Marqeta, which already supported its debit and prepaid programs; the credit card continues to run on the American Express Network. Marqeta deepens its role with an existing customer, while Square brings three card programs onto a common technology provider. Subsequent credit-feature releases and servicing performance will test whether that consolidation delivers Square’s stated goal of faster product development.

perspective: JPMorgan extends deposit tokens to Ethereum as Ramp seeks custody powers, while payment providers expand cross-border distribution and consolidate card infrastructure.

curiosity.text: France introduced Minitel nationally in 1982 and added Kiosque billing in 1984, letting users pay for online services through their telephone bills—years before the World Wide Web. Kiosque’s micropayment model helped make paid online content viable by adding small charges to users’ existing phone bills.
